notes.text: The page continues a statement about a G action on T and displays a map labeled Phi into Hom of groups from T to pi. The domain’s tau/calligraphic-T identification and the first connector’s head remain uncertain. The notation is transcribed as evidence, without proving the construction.

The author describes a homomorphism of the angle-bracketed groupoid into the groupoid of universal coverings of Pi, constant on objects with value tilde Pi. The prose defines the indexed pi sets by lambda t=t prime and identifies the induced maps as inclusions. An interlinear Isom description is attached by a curved guide. Its visible relation is simeq, not the equals sign of witness C. No proof of these assertions was performed.

The closing sentence states compatibility with the action of the unresolved E/Sigma group on a Pi whose possible tilde overlaps the line above, and consequently on pi. Four final suspension marks are present. H’s later compatibles and additional illegible tails are not separate manuscript words after the final pi.

No independently identifiable deletion was found on this page. The interlinear formula is an insertion, and its thin curved attachment stroke is reproduced as a drawing. The pencil 22 is attributed only to an unnamed hand.

The lower diagram describes the category of universal coverings of Pi equal to tilde Pi and then writes a comparison with a single object having isomorphism group pi. The manuscript says un objet, not un seul objet. Its isom--- abbreviation and the restriction égaux followed by the reduced à/colon graph and tilde Pi are retained; égaux is secure and the following mark is now explicitly uncertain.

The opening action statement and Phi map into Hom of groups were checked as written. Its tiny connector remains arrow-first/bare-shaft uncertainty; the plain T arguments remain distinct from the object-set letter. The two reduced à/colon graphs now carry explicit alternatives with à preferred, as independently agreed by main.

The source describes a groupoid homomorphism, constant on objects, with value the covered Pi. The indexed pi definition, lambda condition, inclusion and inserted Isom description are retained. The visible insertion relation is simeq and the thin physical guide is already reproduced. No proof of the stated construction or inclusions was performed.

The seven-line lower target and parenthetical description are retained. Égaux is clear; only its following reduced mark gains uncertainty. The long horizontal returns from égaux and groupe are continuous g descenders and are not added as separate guides or rules. The two isolated low points below the left side of the lower object glyph have no unambiguous punctuation/index attachment and are not supplied as text.

The closing compatibility assertion is retained with its group-letter uncertainty and M0703 Pi/covered-Pi uncertainty. The possible tilde remains entangled with évidemment on the line above. Four terminal points are visible, distinct from the first display’s three. The statement’s mathematics was not used to decide the tilde.

No preferred source reading changes in this audit. Two certainty-only additions revise existing collation rows 1 and 26 rather than create new material rows. All eight existing doubts remain, plus the two à/colon doubts. The only original MARK, M0703, stays undecided. No new source crop, recrop, research, OCR or TeX compilation was used.

raw_difference_disposition:
All 33 packet differences were inspected against the original, both halves and the six single-locus crops. Every word and symbol was also inspected where C and H agree. Pure macro, spacing and editorial-description differences are excluded as source words. For unresolved alternatives, the flags compare the preferred first reading to the witnesses without declaring either certainly wrong. Main-reader review prefers the small arrowhead over the bare shaft at low confidence. Domain alphabet rows are medium-confidence/non-consequential; the pure E/Sigma row is low-confidence/non-consequential. Detailed packet-order disposition:
1. Scan metadata only; not an additional manuscript numeral.
2. Reduced à and Phi label recovered; first displayed map inspected as a whole.
3. Domain alphabet remains tau/calligraphic T; connector head remains open; Hom-gr target recovered.
4. Actual Hom target contains (T,pi); H’s token alignment is incomplete and the full formula was checked visually.

7. Literal rev. retained, not lengthened to revêt.
8. Constant selected from strokes, not construits.

12. Flèches recovered from f, l, accent and ending.
13. Qui is present between et and pour.
14. Membership-condition domain alphabet remains tau/calligraphic T.

16. Simeq selected from the wavy upper stroke, changing C equals.
17. Inserted Isom subscript retains the same unresolved domain alphabet.
18. H’s editorial insertion description is not source prose; the actual addition and curved attachment guide are reconstructed.
19. No period after the second l’ens.
20. Est recovered from its compressed graph and compared with the later est.
21. Comma retained in the lower indexed pi; the low attached return contrasts with the higher prime.
22. Ce foncteur, not Le foncteur.
23. Diagram-environment syntax only.
24. Lower functor domain alphabet remains tau/calligraphic T.

26. Second rev. also remains unexpanded.

31. Closing est évidemment compatible avec op. de recovered; E/Sigma remains shared low-confidence, non-consequential ambiguity.
32. M0703 remains Pi/tilde Pi due overlap with upper line; donc selected over donné.
33. Pencil 22 retained; H’s extra compatibles and illegible tail after the final pi are not source text. Four source points, not three, end the clause.
